meta.title: Onboarding Checklist
meta.description: A floating checklist widget with step dependencies, localStorage persistence, and animated expand/collapse. The get-started widget every SaaS ships — done right.

blocks.content: Every SaaS ships an onboarding checklist. Most are hardcoded arrays rendered in a sidebar, with no step dependencies, no persistence, and no way to skip optional steps. The user completes step 1, refreshes, and it resets. The system handles all of it: step ordering, dependency gates, localStorage persistence, and the animated floating widget.

Steps have a requires field — an array of step ids that must be complete before this step becomes active. The progress ring on the floating trigger reflects only required steps. Optional steps are skippable and don't affect completion.

blocks.title: Persistence is automatic
blocks.content: Step statuses are saved to localStorage under storageKey on every change and restored on mount. Refreshing the page, closing the tab, and coming back all preserve progress. Pass storageKey to namespace it per user if needed.
Complete steps in order. Notice that Invite a teammate is locked until Create your first project is done. Deploy to production is optional — it can be skipped. Progress persists across page reloads.
Wrap your app in ChecklistRoot with your steps. The floating widget renders automatically at the bottom-right. It persists to localStorage under storageKey and restores on mount.

The requires field takes an array of step ids. The step renders as locked (with a padlock icon) and its CTA is disabled until all required steps are marked complete. Steps without requires are always active.
canActivate(id) is exposed via useChecklist if you need to check dependency status in custom UI. It returns true when all required steps are complete or when requires is empty.
Statuses are saved to localStorage automatically. To namespace per user so different users on the same browser don't share state, include the user id in storageKey.
Pass position: 'inline' to suppress the floating widget. Then use children with useChecklist to compose your own layout — embed the checklist in a sidebar, a settings page, or any custom position.
